Singapore · 55 min · 2 portions

Ginger chicken & brown rice

Ginger-and-soy chicken with brown rice, broccoli, carrots, fresh cucumber, spring onion and lime. A Singapore-inspired meal-prep bowl; choose pan or air fryer for the same seasoned chicken.

Cook step by step

Ingredients (makes 2 portions)

  • 140 g dry brown rice
  • 300 g raw skinless chicken breast
  • 300 g broccoli
  • 200 g cucumber
  • 150 g carrots
  • 20 g fresh ginger
  • 2 garlic cloves
  • 10 ml rapeseed oil
  • 15 ml reduced-salt soy sauce
  • 1 lime
  • 2 spring onions
  • 30 ml water (pan method only; add a little more if needed)

Equipment: Rice cooker OR saucepan with lid; air fryer OR non-stick frying pan with lid; saucepan and colander for boiling OR steamer basket and pot; chopping boards, knife, spoon, fine grater, mixing bowl and tongs.

Allergens: Soy; wheat if your soy sauce contains it.

Make it yours: Replace chicken with firm tofu if preferred; recalculate nutrition and check the tofu label. Use tamari labelled gluten-free if needed.

Method

  1. Start the brown rice

    Stovetop (default):

    • Rinse rice. Add water using the packet ratio.
    • Bring to a simmer, cover and cook for the packet time. Prep the other ingredients while it cooks.

    Rice cooker:

    • Rinse rice. Use your cooker’s cup, brown-rice water guide and minimum batch size.
    • Select Brown Rice, or follow your model’s brown-rice instructions. Let the full cycle and rest finish; fluff.

    What it should look like: Tender grains; no hard centre.

  2. Prepare the vegetables
    • Wash produce. Cut broccoli into 3 cm florets and carrots into 3 mm slices.
    • Slice cucumber into half-moons, spring onions thinly and lime into wedges.
    • Chill cucumber, spring onion and lime separately from broccoli and carrots.

    What it should look like: Even broccoli florets and thin carrot slices. Cold toppings kept separate.

  3. Peel & grate the ginger
    • Peel ginger with a spoon.
    • Finely grate into a bowl; keep the juice. Keep fingertips away from the grater.

    What it should look like: Fine, moist ginger shreds.

  4. Finely chop the garlic
    • Peel garlic and finely chop. Tuck fingertips away from the blade.

    What it should look like: Small pieces, not thick slices.

  5. Cut & season the chicken
    • On a separate board, cut chicken into 2.5 cm cubes. Do not rinse it.
    • Toss once with all the measured oil, ginger, garlic and soy. Refrigerate if waiting.
    • Wash hands, board and knife. Use clean utensils for cooked food.

    What it should look like: Even cubes, lightly coated in seasoning.

  6. Cook the ginger chicken

    Pan (default):

    • Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat. Add the seasoned chicken and measured water.
    • Cook in one layer for 8–12 minutes, turning regularly. Check from 8 minutes.
    • Lower heat or add a splash of water if scorching. Use a clean bowl for cooked chicken.

    Air fryer:

    • Preheat to 200°C (about 5 minutes; follow your manual).
    • Add seasoned chicken in one uncrowded layer. Discard leftover raw marinade.
    • Cook 10–12 minutes per batch. Turn at 5 minutes; check from 10 minutes.

    What it should look like: Cut several thick pieces: steaming-hot centre, no pink meat, clear juices. If unsure, cook longer and check again. Browning alone is not enough.

  7. Cook the vegetables

    Steam (default):

    • Use broccoli and carrots already cut in step 2. Place in a basket above boiling water; cover.
    • Steam 5–7 minutes; check from 5 minutes. Remove tender pieces first and drain.
    • Keep water in the pot. Lift the lid away from your face.

    Boil:

    • Add prepared carrots to boiling water. Once boiling again, cook 2 minutes.
    • Add broccoli. Once gently boiling again, cook 4–5 minutes.
    • Fork-check both vegetables, then drain carefully.

    What it should look like: A fork enters carrot and broccoli stems with gentle resistance.

  8. Build and portion your bowls
    • Divide rice, chicken, broccoli and carrots between bowls. Add cooked pan juices if using.
    • Top with cucumber, spring onion and lime. Never reuse raw marinade.
    • Saving for later? Keep cold toppings separate and follow Meal prep.

    What it should look like: Rice topped with chicken, cooked vegetables and fresh toppings.
